name: IL-09
label: Safe D

model.rationale: The D+19 district fundamentals make this a Safe Democratic hold even with Schakowsky retiring, and Biss has raised nearly $3 million while the Republican reports minimal resources. Markets price Democrats around 95%, consistent with a comfortable expected margin in the low 20s.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Biss or an unusually strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement leaves this Chicago-area district open, but the seat remains firmly Democratic territory with a partisan lean of D+19. Daniel Biss enters the general election as a heavy favorite, having raised nearly $3 million for the race and built name recognition through prior statewide and local campaigns. Outside groups have spent on both sides, with slightly more opposing Biss than supporting him, but the scale is modest relative to his own war chest.

Republican John Elleson has reported little in fundraising or cash on hand, leaving him badly outmatched financially. Prediction markets price Democratic odds near 95%, and no general-election polling is available, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals. The expected margin sits in the low 20s, with modest uncertainty from the open-seat dynamic.
